course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: AI Engineering for Smart Agriculture
course.prerequisites: Electrical Engineering and Embedded, Applied Artificial Intelligence, Data Science for Smart Agriculture
course.description: This course focuses on the design and development of end-to-end artificial intelligence systems for smart agriculture. Students will learn how to integrate data pipelines, machine learning models, IoT sensors, and user interfaces into scalable and deployable solutions. Emphasis is placed on real-world constraints such as limited connectivity, resource efficiency, and sustainability. The course culminates in a capstone project where students build and demonstrate a working AI-based agricultural system.

clos.description: Analyse requirements for AI-based system architectures in smart agriculture applications
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lecture, system design workshop, case analysis
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Quiz, Midterm Exam, Project Proposal (system architecture)

clos.description: Evaluate AI models and system performance for scalability, reliability, and real-world constraints
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Case study, performance analysis, problem-based learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Assignment 1 (evaluation), Midterm Exam, Final Project (evaluation & optimization)

clos.description: Develop AI-driven applications integrating data pipelines, sensors, and user interfaces
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Hands-on lab, coding practice, system integration tasks
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Assignment 1 (model integration), Assignment 2 (deployment), Final Project (system implementation)

clos.description: Organize ethical, sustainable, and socially responsible AI solutions in agricultural systems
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Participation (ethics discussion), Final Project (sustainability & impact reflection)

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to AI Systems in Agriculture
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the concept of AI systems in smart agriculture LLO2: Identify real-world applications and challenges in agricultural systems

topics.title: Topic 2: AI System Architecture
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify key components of an AI system (data, model, deployment) LLO2: Design a basic end-to-end system architecture

topics.title: Topic 3: Data Pipelines and Integration
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe data flow from sensors to AI models LLO2: Design a data pipeline for agricultural applications

topics.title: Topic 4: Sensors and IoT in Smart Farming
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify IoT devices and their roles in agriculture LLO2: Integrate sensor data into an AI pipeline LLO3: Evaluate challenges in real-world data collection

topics.title: Topic 5: Model Integration into Systems
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Integrate a machine learning model into a system pipeline LLO2: Analyse challenges in model integration LLO3: Evaluate system performance after integration

topics.title: Topic 6: APIs and Backend for AI Systems
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the role of APIs in AI systems LLO2: Design a simple API for model serving LLO3: Implement basic backend logic for AI applications

topics.title: Topic 7: Dashboards and Visualization
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Interpret outputs from AI systems LLO2: Design a dashboard for agricultural decision-making

topics.title: Topic 8: Real-time and Streaming Systems
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain real-time data processing concepts LLO2: Design a simple streaming pipeline LLO3: Evaluate system performance under real-time conditions

topics.title: Topic 9: Cloud and Edge Deployment
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Compare cloud and edge deployment approaches LLO2: Select appropriate deployment strategies for agricultural contexts LLO3: Evaluate deployment trade-offs (latency, cost, connectivity)

topics.title: Topic 10: System Evaluation and Optimization
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify key performance metrics (latency, accuracy, reliability) LLO2: Evaluate system performance using appropriate metrics LLO3: Propose improvements for system optimization

topics.title: Topic 11: Ethics, Sustainability and AI Governance
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify ethical issues in AI-based agricultural systems LLO2: Analyse sustainability impacts of AI solutions LLO3: Propose responsible and inclusive AI practices

topics.title: Topic 12: Project Proposal and System Design
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Design a complete AI system architecture LLO2: Justify design decisions based on real-world constraints LLO3: Present system proposal clearly

topics.title: Topic 13: System Development
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Develop components of an AI system (pipeline, API, interface) LLO2: Integrate system components into a working prototype

topics.title: Topic 14: Testing and Evaluation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Test system functionality and performance LLO2: Evaluate system against defined criteria LLO3: Recommend improvements based on results

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
